02c5ad3385.q: How did the Central Bank of Ireland building become available for restaurant development?
02c5ad3385.a: The Central Bank of Ireland relocated from the building in 2014 to new premises on the north side of the docks. The entire development was subsequently sold to a company called Heinz, which came up with a plan to redevelop the property.
02c5ad3385.e: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

1e1d05be52.q: What was the timeline from initial agreement to opening for a rooftop restaurant development in Dublin?
1e1d05be52.a: Alan agreed with the development team in early 2021, with negotiations and legal processes taking approximately six to eight months. Designs were completed mid-2023 and were then tendered out, followed by the construction phase on the 18,000 square foot premise.
1e1d05be52.e: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

7b7a44bd12.q: What international rooftop dining experiences influenced the concept for a premium restaurant in Dublin?
7b7a44bd12.a: Alan's biggest influences were Sushi Samba in Dubai at 78 floors up, Delilah in Vegas, Sexy Fish and Carbone in Miami, and Komodo. These venues demonstrated the successful combination of dining, entertainment, and a one-stop night-out experience that hadn't been delivered in Dublin at that level.
7b7a44bd12.e: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

09fcd56fd1.q: How did reaching out to established restaurant designers and operators help shape the final concept?
09fcd56fd1.a: Alan and his colleague Laura reached out to Greg Markel at Eye Crave in New York, who designed Sushi Samba in Dubai. Although Greg initially explained they never work in Europe, he offered Alan and Laura a weekend trip to Ireland. The team came over for three to four days to see the venue and competition, and this in-person engagement resulted in a genuine partnership with comprehensive design support.
09fcd56fd1.e: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

411657cbe0.q: What role does detail and customer experience play in fine dining restaurant operations according to a Dublin rooftop restaurateur?
411657cbe0.a: Alan emphasized that obsession with detail kills him personally and continues even after opening—he remains focused on elements like door weight and overall customer journey. He stated: 'What are we without customers? We're empty. We're out of business. We're nobody. If you don't engage and enjoy them and want to be part with them, I don't think this business is for you.'
411657cbe0.e: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

a5c38f6235.q: How does technology integration like point-of-sale systems support operational efficiency in upscale restaurants?
a5c38f6235.a: Alan found Toast incredibly useful for real-time access to critical business metrics. He can check his restaurant operations in San Diego immediately from anywhere and tracks key performance indicators, particularly the labor cost ratio he calls 'miles per hour'—monitoring staff hours versus turnover continuously since hours spent cannot be recovered and the same staffing is needed the following week.
a5c38f6235.e: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

3921bc06c0.q: What architectural and design principle guided the creation of an inclusive fine dining rooftop restaurant?
3921bc06c0.a: Alan wanted the restaurant to be Irish, accessible, and for everybody—a special occasion venue that could also be for everyday occasions. He didn't want guests to feel they needed to dress formally, and wanted the experience to be comfortable enough for lunch or any visit, not just used once every six months.
3921bc06c0.e: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

d3a99659e4.q: What is the significance of the name Dion for a rooftop restaurant in Dublin and its Gaelic origins?
d3a99659e4.a: Dion is spelled D-I-A-D-H-A-N and is a Gaelic word meaning roof or shelter. Alan chose this name as his very first decision for the entire project, and it was never changed or challenged by anyone involved. It connects to his media career practice of filming on restaurant roofs to tell larger stories across social platforms.
d3a99659e4.e: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

4dce45e5f6.q: How does a restaurateur fund and secure investment for a major rooftop venue development?
4dce45e5f6.a: Alan prepared a detailed presentation to finance the project and initially approached six to eight potential investors for smaller partnership stakes. However, after one investor visited Sushi Samba in Dubai and fully grasped the vision, he offered to fund the entire project without other investors, brought a full team including a financial director, and remained actively supportive through the intensive final weeks before opening.
4dce45e5f6.e: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

4a0d5f4b2d.q: Why is quarterly thinking incompatible with operating a freehold hospitality business?
4a0d5f4b2d.a: Alistair Darby explains that you simply cannot run a freehold hospitality business thinking quarterly—it is insane. The owners of Sir Richard Sutton Limited think in decades, considering what their grandchildren will inherit in 50 years, not tomorrow. This long-term perspective allows the company to make major investments like building a new hotel in Mayfair that will stand for 100 years, decisions that would be impossible under quarterly performance pressures.
4a0d5f4b2d.e: This CEO Says Quarterly Thinking Is “Insane.” His Company Is Building a Hotel Designed to Stand for 100 Years

4b96062fa8.q: How should a CEO's role differ in hospitality organizations?
4b96062fa8.a: Darby rejects the quarterback analogy for a CEO, arguing instead that a CEO's job is to be the linebacker. The quarterback is the person serving a drink, brewing coffee, or tidying a bedroom—the frontline staff. The CEO's job is to protect them and ensure they do not get sacked. This servant leadership approach means spending all time facilitating, enabling, freeing up space, and protecting people so they can focus on their interaction with guests.
4b96062fa8.e: This CEO Says Quarterly Thinking Is “Insane.” His Company Is Building a Hotel Designed to Stand for 100 Years

97436fe30e.q: What business lesson emerged from studying breakfast buffet success in German bars?
97436fe30e.a: Darby recounts meeting Bernd Rieger, an ex-hotelier running successful all-day bars in Germany where breakfast represented 30 percent of daily trade. Rieger explained that when they started, they wasted a lot of food, but they set up the buffet with an entire spread from day one with just one customer, then gradually built their reputation rather than opening with a limited offering. This demonstrated the long-term mindset: accepting short-term pain (wasted food) to build a lasting, superior guest experience.
97436fe30e.e: This CEO Says Quarterly Thinking Is “Insane.” His Company Is Building a Hotel Designed to Stand for 100 Years

71b2051c3c.q: How does customer data reveal what guests actually want versus what they say?
71b2051c3c.a: Darby explains that you can ask a guest or customer a question and get an answer, but it will not be the proper answer—it is the instant answer. True insight requires asking follow-up questions and probing deeper. He illustrates this with a spirits company example where shoppers said they preferred an oval tin for gift packaging, but when asked why, revealed they planned to remove the bottle, wrap it separately, and reuse the tin for pantry storage—a completely different value proposition than what marketers assumed.
71b2051c3c.e: This CEO Says Quarterly Thinking Is “Insane.” His Company Is Building a Hotel Designed to Stand for 100 Years

aa1c562b68.q: What role does curiosity play in effective CEO leadership?
aa1c562b68.a: Darby emphasizes that his longstanding mentor valued natural curiosity above all else when recruiting—the ability to look at a situation, narrow your eyes, and ask if that is really the case. Curiosity drives better decision-making because it leads to genuine inquiry beyond surface-level answers and uncovers what guests truly want. Without curiosity, leaders make assumptions that prove incorrect.
aa1c562b68.e: This CEO Says Quarterly Thinking Is “Insane.” His Company Is Building a Hotel Designed to Stand for 100 Years

cf2e5c6d73.q: How does active listening enhance leadership effectiveness in hospitality?
cf2e5c6d73.a: Darby credits his wife Alex, an executive coach, as a master of active listening who reads what lies behind what is said. He emphasizes that listening is everything in hospitality and is a direct follow-on from curiosity—if you are genuinely curious, you must listen and listen beyond the first and second answers. Good listening requires patience and genuine interest in understanding what others are really communicating.
cf2e5c6d73.e: This CEO Says Quarterly Thinking Is “Insane.” His Company Is Building a Hotel Designed to Stand for 100 Years
